correctness.rationale: The alignment NFA accepts exactly word pairs with a common length-(n−1) subsequence; subset construction gives 27 pair states, triple product 1549 states. Exact matrix iteration verifies 27 and 1549 consecutive zeros of corresponding polynomial-in-M residual sequences. Cayley–Hamilton then forces all later zeros. Closed-form exponential-polynomial candidates satisfy these annihilators and their initial values. Inclusion–exclusion removes repeated vertices and divides by six. Independent direct graph enumeration n=1..4 checks the graph interpretation. The original packaged Python code ran successfully from its actual path.

value.rationale: The four-symbol alphabet is natural for quaternary sequence coding, including DNA alphabets. The exact all-n triangle count and 45/32 leading coefficient sharpen the previously available O_4(4^n n^3 log n) graph-triangle estimate. The already known binary specialization cannot supply the four-symbol coefficients; a new exact 1549-state recurrence certificate is required. This is a motivated graph invariant used in local-sparsity bounds, though no stronger code-size theorem is claimed.
